raw_text:
Here's your Friday news hit, hot off the presses. Grab a coffee, or something stronger – it's been a week.

### Money Talk

- **Norse Atlantic goes bust, another victim of fuel prices.**
  The budget carrier Norse Atlantic filed for bankruptcy and canceled all flights today. Turns out, soaring fuel costs (hello, Iran war) can really mess with your bottom line when you’re trying to offer cheap flights. Another one bites the dust. [S3][S15]
- **Musk pledges more SpaceX shares for American kids.**
  Elon Musk, never one to do things quietly, announced he's doubling down on his promise to donate SpaceX shares to every American child, now pledging two per kid. SpaceX shares jumped 4% today. Seems like the market approves of his unique brand of philanthropy, or maybe it’s just the broader tech rally. [S2][S20]
- **Your energy bill is about to get a 26% hike.**
  Get ready for a nasty surprise in January: energy bills for millions are set to jump by over a quarter. Blame the surge in gas prices, apparently due to that pesky Iran war. Guess we're all turning into expert energy traders, whether we like it or not. [S7][S9]
- **Durable goods are failing faster, costing you more.**
  It's not just you – cars are sputtering, smart TVs are glitching. A new report says consumer products are getting less reliable, even as prices climb. So you’re paying more for stuff that breaks quicker. Capitalism, baby! [S5]
- **Americans are turning into bargain hunters.**
  Consumer spending has been propping up the economy, but don't let that fool you. People are getting picky, trading down, and hunting for deals. The "Black Friday" frenzy is now a month-long "Black November" affair. Smart money's on essentials and deep discounts. [S17][S18]

### World Lore

- **North Korea's Kim doubles down on nukes, ignores Trump.**
  Kim Jong Un reportedly ignored an overture from President Trump and instead vowed to build *more* nuclear weapons. He even toured facilities making the ingredients. Looks like "denuclearization" is still very much a distant dream. Keep those bunkers stocked. [S25]
- **EU budget summit goes sideways, Ukraine funding stalled.**
  Europe is having a tough time with its seven-year budget. Leaders couldn't agree on how to fund Ukraine, and the proposed 3% tax on US tech companies (to generate more funds) is just adding fuel to the fire. Unity? What unity? [S34]
- **Congo's Ebola outbreak escalates amidst fighting.**
  The Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has hit 12,000 cases, with some responders evacuating as fighting between rebels and the army disrupts containment efforts. Just when you think things can’t get worse, war and disease make a terrible combo. [S24]
- **French cinema icon Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape.**
  Gérard Depardieu, a massive figure in French cinema, has been ordered to stand trial on rape and sexual assault charges. This case is a big one for France's #MeToo reckoning, where the movement has faced considerable pushback, especially in the arts. [S21]
- **UN scrambling to find new Secretary General.**
  The current UN Secretary General's term is ending this year, and the big powers are deadlocked on a replacement. Seriously? The world's on fire, and they can't even agree on a new chief firefighter. Don't worry, I'm sure someone will "get up to speed" quickly. [S22]

### Tech Tea

- **Nvidia pauses chip shipments to Southeast Asia amidst US-China tech war.**
  Looks like the US is tightening the screws on AI chips. Nvidia just told its manufacturing partners to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia, all part of the ongoing effort to keep advanced AI tech out of China's hands. The semiconductor chessboard just got more complicated. [S41]
- **Google’s Belgium datacentre construction halted over permits.**
  Belgian authorities have ordered Google to stop work on a massive datacentre. Why? Because the tech giant apparently doesn’t have the right planning permits. Classic Big Tech move, build first, ask questions later (or not at all). Greenpeace is loving it. [S13]
- **Black Friday shoppers beware: WebRTC skimming scripts on popular sites.**
  Cybersecurity folks found credit card skimming scripts, using WebRTC, lurking on popular shopping sites this Black Friday. So while you're hunting for deals, hackers are hunting for your financial data. Maybe just use Apple Pay, or go back to cash? [S40]
- **Convex caught sending user app ideas to remote servers.**
  Developer platform Convex is under fire for allegedly sending users' app ideas to remote servers without explicit consent. In the privacy-conscious tech world, that’s a big no-no. Trust is hard-earned and easily shattered. [S37]
- **X *finally* gets parental controls after 20 years.**
  Elon Musk's X (née Twitter) has at long last added parental controls for teenage users. Twenty years in the making! Glad they got to it before, you know, every child online grew up and had kids of their own. Better late than never, I guess. [S43]

### Creator Szn

- **Fortnite pro "Clix" launches his own holding company.**
  Cody "Clix" Conrod, the Fortnite player with over 26 million followers and nine creator-focused businesses, just launched his own holding company. This isn't just gaming anymore; it's empire-building. Forget venture capital, the real money is in V-bucks and savvy brand deals. [S56]
- **Brands are trying to systematize creator content.**
  As social trends move at warp speed, big brands like General Mills are trying to build systems to score creator posts for "shareability." They want to bridge the gap between organic buzz and paid media. Good luck with that – the internet is chaos, not a spreadsheet. [S57]
- **GTA 6 fuels a massive creator industrial complex.**
  The Grand Theft Auto VI hype machine is in full swing, and it's created an entire "creator industrial complex." Stream numbers, viewership, top creators – everyone's cashing in on the organic buzz. It’s a masterclass in how gaming can print money for everyone involved, not just the developers. [S59]
- **Dick's Sporting Goods turns youth sports into an ad business.**
  Dick’s is betting big on youth sports to fuel its next phase of ad growth through its GameChanger platform. They're basically turning Little League into a premium ad space. Monetizing children's dreams, gotta respect the hustle (or side-eye it, depending on your vibe). [S58]

### Supply Lines

- **UPS acquires Australian healthcare logistics firm Smartways.**
  UPS just snagged Smartways Logistics, beefing up its healthcare supply chain presence in Australia and New Zealand. This move adds couriers reaching ~1,300 hospitals daily, showing UPS is serious about critical, time-sensitive deliveries beyond just parcels. [S71][S72][S73]
- **Amazon's drone delivery expands, but not without a crash.**
  Amazon is rolling out drone delivery in Nashville, promising packages in 30 minutes. But it's not all smooth flying: one drone already crashed into a neighbor's garage, prompting an FAA investigation. Looks like the last mile still has some kinks to work out. [S85][S86]
- **FedEx MD-11 freighter overshoots Miami runway.**
  A FedEx cargo jet ended up in a grassy field after overshooting the runway at Miami airport on Saturday. Thankfully, no serious injuries, but it’s a stark reminder of the risks in air freight operations, especially during stormy weather. [S61][S81][S82]
- **DHL eyes Africa growth, partners with Equity Bank.**
  DHL is dropping €300m into Africa, partnering with Equity Bank and the Chinese Chamber to boost trade and unlock international markets for African SMEs. They’re also seeing growth from first-time outsourcing, which is a smart play in expanding markets. [S74][S76][S77][S78]
- **Grab taps Indonesian startups for AI logistics pilots.**
  Ride-hailing and delivery giant Grab is bringing in five Indonesian startups to pilot AI solutions across its network. This is a clear signal that AI integration, particularly for efficiency and optimization, is the next frontier for last-mile and broader logistics. [S89]
- **Ocean freight rates still double last year, congestion lingers.**
  DHL reports ocean rates are still 138% higher than last year, with a massive 3.6 million TEUs currently stuck in congestion. Shippers are prioritizing resilience over price, which makes sense when your stuff is literally sitting in limbo. [S63]
- **US rail freight sees significant weekly climb, intermodal surges.**
  Good news on the tracks: US freight by rail jumped 4.7% year-over-year, with intermodal volumes surging by an impressive 8.3%. Looks like some capacity is shifting, or demand is just that strong for rail. [S60]
- **Ecommerce air hubs face capacity crunch ahead of Black Friday.**
  Despite the Black Friday rush, air cargo rates are under upward pressure due to *capacity constraints*, not just demand. Freighter capacity into Europe has taken a significant hit, meaning getting your holiday orders by air just got pricier and trickier. [S68]

### Speed Round

- Labour MPs are warning the PM not to block the Rosebank oilfield, claiming it could spell "lights out for Labour in Scotland."
- Trump demanded an investigation into GDP data revisions, alleging understatement without evidence.
- Solo-dining is now a self-care ritual, reshaping the restaurant industry.
- The UN is struggling to find a replacement for its Secretary General, whose term ends this year.
- Marc Marquez, the MotoGP legend, is retiring days after clinching his record 8th world title.
- The iPhone Duo is apparently changing users' habits, from reading more books to breaking mindless scrolling.
- British Gas owner Centrica is seeking urgent government talks to save hundreds of jobs at a gas storage facility.
